title: Theranica of Netanya developed an arm device that relieves migraine without drugs, including for children

trailer.text: Theranica is an Israeli biomedical technology company from Netanya, founded in 2016, that develops electrical treatments for migraine.
Its device, Nerivio, wraps around the upper arm and sends electrical pulses controlled from a smartphone.

In a trial that included 252 patients from 12 clinics (7 in the United States and 5 in Israel), 66.7% of the patients using the active device who were included in the analysis (66 of 99) reported pain relief two hours after treatment, compared with 38.8% (40 of 103) using the sham device.
The FDA expanded the clearance to ages 12 and up in January 2021, and in October 2024 also to children from age eight.
According to the company, Nerivio has been used in more than one million migraine treatments in the U.S.

paragraphs.text: According to Theranica, migraine is a debilitating neurological disease with no cure that affects one billion people worldwide.
According to the company, one in ten children has it.
According to JNS, migraines affect 12 percent of the population in the United States.
Alon Ironi, the CEO and one of the company's founders, says that millions of people still suffer from frequent, debilitating attacks, despite decades of new medications.
The chairman, Dr. Shimon Eckhouse, says that more than half of the 40 million Americans living with migraine are not satisfied with existing treatments.
Prof. Stephen Silberstein of Jefferson in Philadelphia is a member of Theranica's medical advisory board.
According to him, there is a great need for new treatments when existing medications do not help.
He adds that most migraine medications, including over-the-counter drugs, are associated with medication-overuse headache.
According to the research paper, only 15.9% of Americans with migraine use triptans.
Prof. David Yarnitsky notes that most patients are women of reproductive age, and that medications may be a problem in an unplanned pregnancy.

stations.title: The idea: relieving the head through the arm

paragraphs.text: At the time of the study, Prof. David Yarnitsky directed the Department of Neurology at Rambam and headed a laboratory at the Technion.
According to him, the research grew out of his work on pain inhibition using a method called Conditioned Pain Modulation.
The device does not sit on the head or neck, but on the upper arm.
It sends electrical pulses controlled from a smartphone to create this pain-relief response.
Users operate it themselves, through an app.
Each treatment lasts 45 minutes.
To treat an attack, the device is used at its start; for prevention, it is used every other day.
Each device is good for 12 treatments, after which a new device can be obtained by prescription.
According to the researchers, to their knowledge this is the first attempt to use this method to treat pain without drugs and without entering the body.
The authors wrote that the treatment is discreet and convenient, and that daily routine can continue during it.

stations.title: The trial: 252 patients in the United States and Israel

paragraphs.text: The trial on which the clearance was based was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled and multi-center.
It included 252 patients from 12 clinics, 7 in the United States and 5 in Israel.
126 received an active device, and 126 received a sham device.
The first patient was enrolled in December 2017, and the last completed the blinded phase in October 2018.
Dr. Brian Grosberg of Hartford Healthcare in Connecticut was the lead investigator.
Two hours after treatment, 66.7% of the patients in the active group who were included in the analysis (66 of 99) reported pain relief, compared with 38.8% (40 of 103) in the sham group.
The advantage was also sustained 48 hours after treatment.
The symptom that bothered them most was relieved after two hours in 46.3%, compared with 22.2% on placebo.
Device-related side effects occurred in 6 of 126 in the active group, and in 3 of 126 on placebo.
They were mild, resolved within 24 hours and did not require medical treatment.
According to the paper, the device's therapeutic gain is higher than that of transcranial magnetic stimulation and of vagus nerve stimulation.
According to Yarnitsky, the big surprise was that the relief is similar to that of triptans, but he is not sure the mechanism is shared.
Ronen Jashek, a co-founder, said that around two-thirds of patients got significant relief.
On May 28 the company announced that the U.S. FDA had cleared Nerivio Migra.
The clearance was for treating a migraine attack, with or without aura, in adults who do not have chronic migraine.
Ironi said in 2019 that the company was preparing to launch the device in the U.S. at an affordable price.
He said that at least seven other painful conditions had been identified that the technology may relieve, after appropriate clinical development.
In January 2021 Theranica announced that the FDA had expanded the clearance to ages 12 and up, with episodic or chronic migraine.
The adolescent study included 45 adolescents.
After two hours, 71% of the participants included in this figure (28 of 39) achieved pain relief, and 35% (14 of 39) were pain-free.
According to a statement from Theranica, 37% of school-age children do poorly in school because of headaches, and their social lives are also harmed.
In October 2022 Theranica reported positive results in a pivotal trial for migraine prevention.
Those who used the device every other day had on average 4.0 fewer migraine days per month, compared with 1.3 in the placebo group.
Only one mild device-related side effect was reported, and it was in the placebo group.
According to MobiHealthNews, the company received FDA clearance to use Nerivio for migraine prevention in ages 12 and up.
The company raised $35 million in 2019.
The next round, of $45 million, was led by New Rhein Healthcare Investors.
Omron Ventures joined the company's $35 million Series B round as a strategic investor, and the sum of its investment was not disclosed.
According to Globes, trials and real-world studies have shown Nerivio to be comparable to standard pharmacological treatments.

stations.title: Children from age eight, and a million treatments

paragraphs.text: In October 2024 the FDA expanded the clearance to children aged eight and up.
The company announced this on November 14, 2024.
The expansion followed a study that showed, with real-world data, that the treatment is safe and effective also for children aged 6 to 11.
The study included 293 children, most of them girls, with a median age of 11.

Among the children who voluntarily reported their condition at the start of treatment and two hours after it, 72.2% reported pain relief, 36% reported pain freedom and 83.3% reported relief from functional disability, in at least 50% of treatments.
According to Ironi, until now there were very few options for treating migraine in children under 12.
Dr. Daniel Lax said that the FDA decision may open the door to considering the device as a first-line treatment for children and adolescents.
According to Theranica, at one point the device served more than 35,000 people in the U.S., including adolescents and veterans.
According to the company, by 2024 it had been used in more than one million treatments in the U.S.
TIME magazine chose Nerivio for its list of the 100 best inventions.
According to JNS, the device does not cure, so the pain eventually comes back.
In the main study, the researchers noted that it is difficult to build a placebo device that properly conceals the difference in trials of this kind.
They also noted that few participants had severe pain at the start of the attack, and many had mild pain, presumably because they treated early.
They further wrote that the comparisons with triptans and other devices were not made in head-to-head trials against the device.
Some of the researchers are connected to the company.
Alon Ironi, Dagan Harris and Tamar Lin, co-authors of the paper, are Theranica employees.
Prof. Yarnitsky, the first author, serves on the company's medical advisory board.

claims.text: ההרחבה באה אחרי מחקר שהראה בנתוני עולם אמיתי בטיחות ויעילות של הטיפול בילדים בני 6 עד 11.
claims.quote: Real-world data demonstrated the safety and efficacy of remote electrical neuromodulation (REN) for migraine treatment in children aged six to 11.

claims.text: במחקר שפורסם ב-Annals of the Child Neurology Society השתתפו 293 ילדים (73.7% בנות) בגיל חציוני 11.
claims.quote: there were 293 children (73.7% girls) in the study with a median age of 11 years

claims.text: במחקר זה 72.2% מהמטופלים דיווחו על הקלה בכאב, 36% על היעדר כאב ו-83.3% על הקלה בנכות התפקודית.
claims.quote: In all, 72.2% of patients reported pain relief, 36% reported pain freedom, 83.3% reported functional disability relief

claims.text: לדברי אירוני, האפשרויות לטיפול במיגרנה בילדים מתחת לגיל 12 היו מוגבלות מאוד עד כה.
claims.quote: The options for treating migraine in children under 12, especially ones that are safe, drug-free, and can be used for both acute and preventive treatment have been very limited until now.

claims.text: לדברי ד"ר דניאל לקס, החלטת ה-FDA עשויה לפתוח פתח לשקול את הטיפול כקו ראשון לילדים ונוער.
claims.quote: this FDA decision should open the door for considering this therapy as a first-line treatment for children and adolescents

claims.text: לפי Theranica, Nerivio משרת כבר מעל 35,000 אנשים עם מיגרנה בארה"ב, כולל בני נוער ולוחמים משוחררים.
claims.quote: already serves over 35,000 people with migraine in the USA, including adolescents and veterans

claims.text: לפי JNS, הכאב חוזר בסופו של דבר כי הטיפול אינו מרפא.
claims.quote: The pain does come back eventually because this is not a cure.

claims.text: החוקרים ציינו כי בחירת מכשיר פלצבו מתאים להסוואה בניסויי נוירומודולציה למיגרנה היא אתגר גדול.
claims.quote: Finally, selecting an appropriate sham device for successful blinding in neuromodulation studies in migraine is a great challenge.

claims.text: המחברים ציינו כמגבלה שיעור נמוך של כאב בסיס חמור ושיעור גבוה של כאב קל, כנראה בגלל טיפול מוקדם.
claims.quote: First, there was a low rate of severe baseline pain intensity and high rate of mild pain intensity, presumably due to the early treatment.

claims.text: המחברים ציינו שההשוואות לטריפטנים ולמכשירים אחרים אינן מחקרי ראש בראש עם REN.
claims.quote: Limitations of these comparisons are that they are not a head to head trials with REN

claims.text: אלון אירוני, דגן האריס ותמר לין הם עובדי Theranica.
claims.quote: Alon Ironi, Dagan Harris and Tamar Lin are employees of Theranica Ltd.

claims.text: דוד ירניצקי מכהן בוועדה הרפואית המייעצת של Theranica.
claims.quote: David Yarnitsky serves on the Medical Advisory Board of Theranica Ltd

claims.text: לפי NeurologyLive, במחקר הנוער נמצאה תופעת לוואי אחת הקשורה למכשיר (2%): תחושת כאב זמנית בזרוע.
claims.quote: found there to be only 1 device-related adverse event (AE; 2%) which was a temporary feeling of pain in the arm

claims.text: לפי ה-Jerusalem Post, במחקר הנוער לא דווחו תופעות לוואי מזיקות.
claims.quote: No harmful side effects were reported in the study.

claims.text: MobiHealthNews דיווח כי Theranica נוסדה ב-2016 וקיבלה 45 מיליון דולר במימון סבב C באוגוסט.
claims.quote: Founded in 2016, Theranica announced it had received $45 million in Series C funding in August.

claims.text: באוקטובר 2024 הרחיב ה-FDA את האישור לילדים מגיל שמונה ומעלה.
